I am old now, 83 years, but my hands still know the land. Five mu is all I have, and with only me and my wife at home, I do what I have always done. My son helps bring in the harvest, but the rest is mine.

For the wheat, I sow in October like every year. I use the improved seed from the agricultural station in town — the dealer sells the same variety most people here plant, and last year it gave me almost 450 kg per mu, so I keep with it. Before sowing, I spread two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 kg each) per mu as base. That is one bag for two mu... no, wait, I mean two bags for one mu. My memory is not what it was, but my hands remember. Then in spring, at jointing time, I topdress with urea, about one small bag — 20 kg — per mu. Irrigation I do three times from the well: once before winter so the roots settle, once at jointing in March, and once when the grain is filling if the sky does not give rain. Pesticide I spray twice, once for aphids and once for the rust when I see the leaves yellowing.

For the maize, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. I do not plough — I just use rotary, it saves the tractor fee. The seed I buy is hybrid, the Zhengdan type most neighbors use. Base fertilizer is one bag of compound per mu at sowing, then I topdress urea twice — once when knee-high, once before tasseling — maybe 25 kg of urea total per mu. Potassium I do not add separately; the compound fertilizer has some. I irrigate twice from the well, at tasseling and grain-filling. Pesticide maybe two times for the borer.

I could spend less on fertilizer, but a bad harvest scares me more than wasting a few yuan. Better too much than too little.
